dmm-2022-power-01a.prompt: In an election, each voter ranks all candidates from most to least preferred. The *Borda score* of a candidate $c$ for a voter $v$ is the rank $r_v(c)$ of $c$ in $v$'s ranking ($1$ for the most preferred), and the Borda score of $c$ is its average rank over all voters. The candidate with the smallest Borda score wins; ties are broken arbitrarily (you cannot break ties in your favour). There are three voters and three candidates Xavier, Yisa and Zack, whose rankings are: Alice: Xavier $>$ Yisa $>$ Zack, Bob: Zack $>$ Xavier $>$ Yisa, Cady: Yisa $>$ Xavier $>$ Zack (for instance Alice prefers Xavier the most and Zack the least). The Borda score of Zack is $\frac{1+3+3}{3}=\frac73$. Compute the Borda scores of Xavier and Yisa, and explain why Xavier wins.
dmm-2022-power-01a.answer: Xavier $\frac53$, Yisa $2$; Xavier has the smallest score.

dmm-2022-power-03a.prompt: There are $n$ voters and $m$ candidates; $r_v(c)$ is the rank of candidate $c$ for voter $v$ ($1$ is the best). A *committee* is a set $T$ of candidates. Its Borda score for voter $v$ is $r_v(T)=\min_{c\in T}r_v(c)$, and its Borda score is $r_{\mathcal V}(T)=\frac1n\sum_vr_v(T)$ (the average over voters of the best rank in the committee). Consider the election with five voters $v_1,\dots,v_5$ and five candidates $c_1,\dots,c_5$ with preferences $v_1:c_1>c_2>c_3>c_4>c_5$, $v_2:c_2>c_1>c_4>c_3>c_5$, $v_3:c_5>c_2>c_1>c_3>c_4$, $v_4:c_3>c_4>c_2>c_5>c_1$, $v_5:c_4>c_1>c_2>c_3>c_5$. Find the committee of size $2$ with the smallest Borda score, and compute its Borda score.

dmm-2022-power-03b.prompt: There are $n$ voters and $m$ candidates; $r_v(c)$ is the rank of candidate $c$ for voter $v$ ($1$ is the best). A *committee* is a set $T$ of candidates. Its Borda score for voter $v$ is $r_v(T)=\min_{c\in T}r_v(c)$, and its Borda score is $r_{\mathcal V}(T)=\frac1n\sum_vr_v(T)$ (the average over voters of the best rank in the committee). Given an election, let $T^*_k$ denote a committee of size $k$ with the smallest Borda score. Is it necessarily true that $T^*_k\subset T^*_{k+1}$? Prove your answer.

dmm-2022-power-03c.prompt: There are $n$ voters and $m$ candidates; $r_v(c)$ is the rank of candidate $c$ for voter $v$ ($1$ is the best). A *committee* is a set $T$ of candidates. Suppose we select $k$ candidates uniformly at random (among all $\binom mk$ subsets of the $m$ candidates) to form a committee $T$. What is the expected value $\mathbf E[r_{\mathcal V}(T)]$ of the Borda score of $T$? Express your answer in terms of $n,m,k$ and prove it.

dmm-2022-power-04a.prompt: There are $n$ voters and $m$ candidates; $r_v(c)$ is the rank of candidate $c$ for voter $v$ ($1$ is the best). A *committee* is a set $T$ of candidates. Its Borda score for voter $v$ is $r_v(T)=\min_{c\in T}r_v(c)$, and its Borda score is $r_{\mathcal V}(T)=\frac1n\sum_vr_v(T)$ (the average over voters of the best rank in the committee). Build committees $\emptyset=T_0\subsetneq T_1\subsetneq\dots\subsetneq T_k$ greedily: in round $j$, pick the candidate $c_j\notin T_{j-1}$ that minimizes $r_{\mathcal V}(T_{j-1}\cup\{c_j\})$ (ties broken arbitrarily); call this procedure Greedy. Consider the election with five voters $v_1,\dots,v_5$ and five candidates $c_1,\dots,c_5$ with preferences $v_1:c_1>c_2>c_3>c_4>c_5$, $v_2:c_2>c_1>c_4>c_3>c_5$, $v_3:c_5>c_2>c_1>c_3>c_4$, $v_4:c_3>c_4>c_2>c_5>c_1$, $v_5:c_4>c_1>c_2>c_3>c_5$. For $k=3$, compute the committee that Greedy produces.
dmm-2022-power-04a.answer: $\{c_1,c_2,c_4\}$ (one of several tied choices in the last round: $\{c_2,c_4,c_1\}$, $\{c_2,c_4,c_3\}$, $\{c_2,c_4,c_5\}$ all have score $\frac75$).
dmm-2022-power-04a.reviewNote: In round 3, c1, c3 and c5 tie (score 7/5), so Greedy's committee depends on tie-breaking; the official answer {c1,c2,c4} is one valid outcome.

dmm-2022-power-04c.prompt:
There are $n$ voters and $m$ candidates; $r_v(c)$ is the rank of candidate $c$ for voter $v$ ($1$ is the best). A *committee* is a set $T$ of candidates. Its Borda score for voter $v$ is $r_v(T)=\min_{c\in T}r_v(c)$, and its Borda score is $r_{\mathcal V}(T)=\frac1n\sum_vr_v(T)$ (the average over voters of the best rank in the committee). Build committees $\emptyset=T_0\subsetneq T_1\subsetneq\dots\subsetneq T_k$ greedily: in round $j$, pick the candidate $c_j\notin T_{j-1}$ that minimizes $r_{\mathcal V}(T_{j-1}\cup\{c_j\})$ (ties broken arbitrarily); call this procedure Greedy. Let $T_j$ be the committee after $j$ rounds ($1\le j<m$) and write $r_v(T_j)$ and $r_{\mathcal V}(T_j)$ for its Borda scores. Prove that

Let $\mathrm{Rand}(k)=\frac{m+1}{k+1}$ be the expected Borda score of a random committee of size $k$ (Problem 3(c)). dmm-2022-power-06a.prompt: There are $n$ voters and $m$ candidates; $r_v(c)$ is the rank of candidate $c$ for voter $v$ ($1$ is the best). A *committee* is a set $T$ of candidates. Its Borda score for voter $v$ is $r_v(T)=\min_{c\in T}r_v(c)$, and its Borda score is $r_{\mathcal V}(T)=\frac1n\sum_vr_v(T)$ (the average over voters of the best rank in the committee). The *$s$-Borda score* of a committee $T$ is $r_{\mathcal V}(T)=\frac1n\sum_{v\in\mathcal V}\left(\min_{Q\subseteq T,\ |Q|=s}\sum_{c\in Q}r_v(c)\right)$. Interpret this definition in plain English.
dmm-2022-power-06a.answer: For each voter take the $s$ best-ranked committee members, add their ranks; then average over voters.
